- When sentiment is high (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high.
- If sentiment is low (≤ 0.25) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or negative; apply a 0.8–1.2% upward bias for low sentiment periods.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in early 30-day window (days 1–7); adjust downward by 0.5–1.0% for first 7 days if sentiment is flat or negative.
- If sentiment spikes to 1.00, model often fails to adjust downward; apply a 1–2% downward correction if sentiment peaks and prices fall.
